maps.summary:
I ran a boundary anatomy of the adopted preset geoset_rep_x on DEV-A only. Inputs were the masks in stage1/geomem/runs/_e13_dev and the pair list in its dev_pairs.json; the keyframe and DEV-B were never touched. My J&F recomputation matches dev_pairs.json exactly (max |dJF| = 0) on all 3 300 pairs. Good seeds are the 3 007 pairs with J&F >= 0.8.

Good seeds score J 0.9003, F 0.9729, J&F 0.9366 (scene-cluster 95% CI 0.9301 to 0.9433), so the gap is 0.0634. 1-recall is 0.0637 and 1-precision 0.0418.

**Band oracles.** Replacing the prediction by the GT inside the band around the GT boundary gives:
- ±1 px: 0.9649, closes 44.7% of the gap
- ±2 px: 0.9767 (CI 0.9735 to 0.9800), closes 63.3% (CI 61.3 to 65.6%)
- ±4 px: 0.9854, closes 76.9%
- ±8 px: 0.9900, closes 84.2%

**Under- vs over-coverage.**
- Under-coverage dominates. Fixing only the missed pixels (FN) inside ±2 px gains +0.0260; fixing only the extra pixels (FP) gains +0.0140. Their difference is +0.0120 (CI 0.0086 to 0.0159).
- FN are 71.7% of the error pixels inside the ±2 px band.
- Masks sit on average 0.53 px inside the true boundary.
- The direction depends on size. Objects under 2k px are balanced (net -0.02 px), and those under 25 grid cells are slightly over-covered (+0.13 px). Objects of 100k px or more are under-covered by 0.64 px, with FN making up 75% of their in-band error.
- People and other moving objects ('dynamic' type) are the most under-covered (FN share 0.795).
- Walls and floors ('env' type) have the most error outside the band: the ±2 px oracle closes only 58% of their gap, and their F is 0.905.

**Image border.** Not a major factor.
- Objects that touch the frame score J&F 0.9338, against 0.9380 for those that don't.
- The ±2 px oracle restricted to the band within 16 px of the frame gains +0.0040, against +0.0367 beyond 16 px.
- Within 4 px of the frame the error rate is slightly higher (0.391 vs 0.354 per band pixel) and leans towards FP (FN share 0.545).

**Neighbouring objects.** The DEV GT label maps are fully dense: only 35 unlabelled pixels exist in all 170 views, so the "unlabelled background" case effectively does not occur.
- 96.9% of good-seed GT boundary pixels border another seeded (decoded) object; 3.1% border a labelled object that was not decoded.
- The ±2 px oracle restricted to the shared-with-seeded parts recovers 98.5% of the full band gain.
- The 302 pairs that touch an undecoded object score lower (J&F about 0.918 vs 0.939).

**The predicted masks leave gaps.** Treating each view's masks as one partition shows where the misses come from.
- 6.67% of all view pixels are claimed by no mask; 58.8% of those belong to a seeded object.
- Good-seed error pixels split into:
  - FN that no mask claims: 51.3% (CI 44.3 to 58.7%)
  - FN taken by a neighbour's mask: 20.5%
  - FP on a seeded neighbour: 23.4%
  - FP on an undecoded object: 4.9%
- Inside ±2 px the split is 45.1 / 26.6 / 27.0 / 1.2%.
- 44% of the unclaimed FN lie within 2 px of a claimed pixel, i.e. thin seams between masks.
- The exclusivity step (xcl) cannot create unclaimed pixels; they come from the threshold at 0.

**Gap-filling probe.** Giving each unclaimed pixel to the nearest mask (no GT used) picks the right object only 65% of the time.
- k = 1 px: +0.0014 (CI 0.0006 to 0.0027)
- k = 2 px: +0.0009
- unlimited distance: -0.0102
- The ceiling (unclaimed pixels within 2 px given to their true owner) is +0.0170 (CI 0.0144 to 0.0199).

**288-grid round trip of the GT.** J&F 0.9845 (CI 0.9820 to 0.9870). Its shortfall, 0.0155, is 24.5% (CI 20.8 to 27.5%) of the gap. The 576 grid gives 0.9936 (10.0% of the gap).
- Only 5.9% of the prediction's error pixels coincide with the round trip's error pixels.
- The grid matters most for small objects: 51.9% of the gap under 25 grid cells, against 13.9% at 100k px or more.

**Caveat on F.** The F part of the band oracles falls as the band widens (0.9943 → 0.9908). This is an artefact of the seams the oracle creates at the band edge, so the J-oracles are the cleaner measure.

**Not measured.** I did not re-measure the E10 zoom or E11 xcl effects on DEV-A; that needs two DEV-A decodes on the GPU, which I did not run. Those effects are still known only on the keyframe, and no keyframe number was used here.

Scripts and outputs are kept in stage1/geomem/runs/_e14_boundary-anatomy/ (git-ignored), with scratch copies in the scratchpad's boundary-anatomy folder. No tracked files were modified.

implications: The good-seed gap on DEV-A (0.0634) is mostly area (J): J gap 0.0997 vs F gap 0.0271. The ±2 px band oracle closes 63%. Boundary methods can be designed and checked on DEV-A alone, with no keyframe number used.

Under-coverage is the larger half: fixing only misses gains +0.026, fixing only extras +0.014, and the net boundary sits 0.53 px inside. The direction depends on size: objects under 25 grid cells are over-covered (+0.13 px) while objects of 100k px or more are under-covered (-0.64 px). A uniform dilate or threshold shift therefore cancels out. Any shift rule would have to depend on size or type, and must be chosen on DEV-A and confirmed once on DEV-B.

Boundaries are a multi-object partition problem. The GT is fully dense and 97% of good-seed boundary pixels are shared with another decoded object. The single largest error class is pixels no mask claims (51% of good-seed error pixels, 45% inside ±2 px), all coming from the threshold at 0. The rest is boundaries misplaced between two decoded neighbours (one mask's miss is the other's extra, about 27% each inside the band).

Filling seams on binary masks alone is weak: nearest-mask assignment is right only about 65% of the time, so it gains +0.0014 at k = 1 against a +0.017 ceiling at k = 2. A fill that uses the decoder logits could get closer to that ceiling: give a pixel whose logits are all below 0 to the highest-logit object when that logit is above -tau. This needs per-object logits on DEV-A (another agent is dumping logits under _e14_logitdump). tau must be chosen on DEV-A and confirmed on DEV-B.

Grid resolution is a minority cause. The 288-grid ceiling of the GT explains 24.5% [20.8, 27.5%] of the gap, and only 5.9% of the prediction's error pixels coincide with the grid round trip's errors. Doubling the grid (2× zoom) could reach at most about 0.0155 - 0.0064 = +0.009 on good seeds, concentrated in small objects (grid share 52% under 25 cells, 14% at 100k px or more).

The image border is not a lever: only about 10% of the ±2 px band gain lies within 16 px of the frame. Walls and floors (env type) and objects next to undecoded objects carry error outside the band (the ±2 px oracle closes only 58% for env), which is coverage extent rather than boundary placement.

The zoom (E10) and exclusivity (E11) effects are still keyframe-only; I ran no DEV-A decode for them. To measure them on DEV-A, decode the geoset_rep and geoset_rep_z2r presets on DEV-A with methods.geomem.dev_decode --root geomem/runs/_e14_<name>/<preset>_A. Then rerun bd_anatomy.py and bd_partition.py with --pairs geomem/runs/_e13_dev/dev_pairs.json, and the reports with --good-from anat_geoset_rep_x_A.json.

maps.summary:
I dumped the round-2 decoder outputs for preset geoset_rep_x on DEV-A (85 frames, 170 eval views = 2 per frame, 3952 object-views, which covers all 3300 scored pairs). The decode path was left unchanged. Re-thresholding the saved fp16 low_res through the adopted path gives the adopted DEV-A PNGs byte for byte: 3952/3952 object-views and 3300/3300 pairs, 0 differing pixels. I checked this three ways: inside the dump job, in a separate fresh GPU process that reads only from disk, and on the host with a numpy emulation of the CUDA interpolate. That numpy emulation is bit-exact, so other agents can run post-decode variants on the host without a GPU. I did not touch the TEST keyframe or DEV-B, and I changed no tracked files.

Root: /home/sjpark/Documents/SCSegmentation/stage1/geomem/runs/_e14_logitdump/geoset_rep_x_A/ (1.81 GiB). It has the same layout as dev_decode, so dev_score can read it: <scene>/<t:06d>/<cam>/<obj>.png, _r1/, config.json, round1_conf.json, xcl_conf.json. In addition, each frame has a _logits/ folder with, for each eval camera:
- <cam>.npz: objects int32 [B], hw int32 [2], low_res float16 [B,288,288], ious float32 [B], presence float32 [B], token int8 [B], stability float32 [B]. low_res is exactly the out["low_res"] that decode_scene used: -1024 where presence <= 0, and the stability-selected token. token 0 is the single-mask token; 1..3 mean the decoder fell back to a multimask candidate because token 0's stability was below 0.98.
- <cam>_mm.npz: mm_low_res float16 [B,4,288,288] holds all 4 decoder tokens before the -1024 replacement (0 = single-mask, 1..3 = multimask candidates); mm_ious float32 [B,4] holds their IoUs.
- meta.json and DONE.

The root also holds the summary files index.json, dump_meta.json, verify_torch.json, verify_numpy.json and probe_emul.json. Field definitions are in the docstring of code/e14dump.py.

How the capture works without changing the decode:
- GeoMemStar.decode_view is wrapped. A top-level call with `chunk` is round 2 (decode_scene passes chunk only there). Each round-2 call is matched to its camera through the backbone dict that the camera's round-1 call used, and that round-1 call is identified by the path of the sam3_io.load_image call just before it.
- The tracker's MaskDecoder.predict_masks is wrapped to keep all 4 token masks and IoUs.
- The stability score is recomputed with the decoder's own _get_stability_scores on the same tensor.

Decoder settings in this image: torch 2.10.0+cu128 on an RTX 6000 Ada; dynamic_multimask_via_stability=True, delta 0.05, thresh 0.98, decoder in eval mode.

Reuse API (code/e14dump.py):
- E.load(root, scene, t, cam, mm=False) and E.views(root) read the dump.
- E.masks_torch(low_res, hw) is the exact adopted path on GPU.
- E.logits_full_np(low_res, hw) returns the full-resolution float32 logits on the host; E.masks_numpy(low_res, hw) adds threshold and exclusivity. Both reproduce the adopted output exactly.
- E.exclusive_masks_np reproduces run.exclusive_masks with the 0.5 cap.
- E.read_png_masks and E.dev_pairs are helpers for reading masks and pairs.

implications: Post-decode variants (re-threshold, other upsampling, candidate selection, exclusivity rules) can run entirely on the host from this dump. E.logits_full_np reproduces the adopted full-resolution logits bit for bit and E.masks_numpy reproduces the adopted DEV-A masks with 0 px difference. So any change in DEV-A J&F comes from the variant itself, not from the reproduction.

Use the 3 multimask candidates with care. The decoder only falls back to them on 133 of the 3300 pairs (4.0%). A candidate-selection variant reaches more pairs only if it overrides token 0 on stable objects. mm_low_res is stored before the -1024 replacement, so absent objects still carry raw candidate logits.

The dump stops at the 288 low-res grid. The 1008 map and the image-resolution map are just two bilinear stages of it. Variants that need sub-288 information (decoder features, upscaled embeddings, image edges) still need the image or a new GPU pass; the 288 logits alone cannot supply it.

The emulation's bit-exactness was measured on torch 2.10.0+cu128 CUDA on an RTX 6000 Ada. If the image or torch version changes, re-run probe_emul.py and verify_dump.py --mode numpy before relying on host identity.
Only preset geoset_rep_x on DEV-A is dumped, round 2 of the eval cameras only. Round-1 logits, DEV-B and the TEST keyframe were not decoded, so the protocol's DEV-B confirmation is still unspent.
The dump root is also a complete dev_decode root whose PNGs are byte-identical to _e13_dev. dev_score and dev_compare can use it directly, and _e13_dev/dev_pairs.json stays the baseline scoring.

I tested three host-side post-decode variants of the adopted geoset_rep_x round-2 decode, on DEV-A only, using the logit dump. The TEST keyframe and DEV-B were never touched, no GPU was used, and no tracked file was changed. Grids and the selection rule were written down and hashed before anything was scored: PREREG.md, stamped 2026-10-15T20:33:21+09:00.

**Pipeline check.** Every variant goes 288 logits → upsampler → full-res logits → pos = L > -tau → the adopted exclusivity (argmax winner, nested-mask cap 0.5) → J&F per pair.
- With the adopted upsampler at tau = 0 the pipeline reproduces the adopted PNGs exactly: 0 differing pixels for every object in all 170 views.
- It also reproduces dev_pairs.json J&F exactly on all 3 300 pairs (max |d| = 0).
- I check the per-object crop shortcut on 3 views (all gf settings, bic1, one jbu setting, all 11 taus): 0 differing pixels.

**Selection rule (pre-registered).** Pick by the DEV-A all-pair J&F, aggregated the way dev_compare does (pair → view "t/cam" → scene; 17 scenes). The CIs are the scene-cluster paired bootstrap (10 000 resamples, seed 0). Good seeds are pairs where the adopted J&F is at least 0.8 (3 007 pairs); failing seeds are the other 293. "Hier" means the dev_compare-style aggregate; "pair-mean" is the plain mean over pairs.

**(a) Global threshold shift.** The pick is tau = +1 logit (masks grow; a median boundary moves about 0.8 px).
- All pairs: +0.00314 [+0.00054, +0.00590]. J +0.0041 with a CI above zero; F +0.0022 with a CI that includes zero.
- Good seeds: +0.00168 [-0.00078, +0.00359] hier, so the CI includes zero; +0.00252 pair-mean. That is about 4% of the 0.0634 good-seed gap.
- Failing seeds: +0.01119 [+0.00488, +0.02012].
- Risk: 132 pairs drop by more than 0.01 (114 good, 18 failing), against 358 that rise by more than 0.01. 13 of 17 scenes go up; Dog drops 0.009.
- Selection bias is small: picking tau on 16 scenes and scoring the held-out one gives +0.00288.
- The optimum is flat. tau = +0.5 gives +0.0028 with a tighter CI [+0.0013, +0.0047] and only 78 drops.

**(b) Upsampling alone (no shift).** Nothing beats the adopted bilinear.
- Bicubic: -0.00029 [-0.00097, +0.00045]; on good seeds -0.00067.
- Joint-bilateral upsampling of the logits with the image as guide: the stronger the image guidance, the worse the result. Its best setting is the spatial-only control (no image guidance at all), at -0.00042 [-0.00086, -0.00003].
- Guided filter of the logits: at best -0.00126 [-0.00305, +0.00015].

**(c) Upsampler plus shift.** The joint pick is spatial-only JBU (no image guidance) with tau = +1: +0.00308 [+0.00051, +0.00579]. That is no better than the shift alone: paired difference -0.0001 [-0.0004, +0.0003]. Every upsampler's best tau was +1.

**Why the shift helps.** At tau = +1, 99.4% of the pixels it adds were claimed by no mask at tau = 0, and it removes none. So it is a logit-based fill of the gaps between masks, not a way of moving boundaries. It claims 51% of those unclaimed pixels, but gives them to the right object only 59.7% of the time (65.6% at tau = +0.5). That is no more accurate than the binary nearest-mask fill (about 65%). Of the added pixels, 30% belong to another decoded object's GT and 12% to objects that were not decoded.

implications: A global threshold shift of tau = +1 is the only variant here whose CI on all DEV-A pairs excludes zero (+0.0031 [+0.0005, +0.0059]). It is not a boundary-placement fix: the good-seed gain is +0.0017 hier (CI includes 0) or +0.0025 pair-mean, about 4% of the 0.0634 gap and about 6% of the ±2 px band oracle. Most of the gain is on failing seeds (+0.011 hier, +0.015 pair-mean) and on objects of 100k px or more (+0.0055).

Mechanically, the shift fills the gaps between masks using the logits: 99.4% of the added pixels were unclaimed, and exclusivity stops it from taking pixels another mask already holds. The owner it picks is right only about 60% of the time, no better than the nearest-mask fill. Going beyond about +0.003 toward the +0.017 oracle-fill ceiling needs a better cue for who owns a gap pixel than raw logit height. Ideas: per-object logit calibration, or the multimask candidates in the dump.

Upsampling the 288 logits is not a lever on DEV-A. Bicubic is neutral. Image-guided JBU and guided filtering of the logits get worse the stronger the image guidance, and every edge-aware setting is below the adopted bilinear. Image colour edges do not supply the sub-288 boundary information. Together with the round-trip result in the anatomy, this points away from post-hoc upsampling and toward decoder-side resolution (e.g. zoom) or a learned refinement, if the grid is pursued at all.
Combining an upsampler with the shift adds nothing (-0.0001 [-0.0004, +0.0003] vs the shift alone), so a registration would be the shift alone on the adopted upsampler.

If it is registered: by the pre-registered rule the DEV-A pick is tau = +1. Risk is 132 of 3 300 pairs down by more than 0.01, and the Dog scene drops 0.009. tau = +0.5 has almost the same mean (+0.0028), a tighter CI [+0.0013, +0.0047] and fewer drops (78); the two differ by only +0.0003 [-0.0009, +0.0013]. Choosing 0.5 now would be a post-hoc change, so it would have to be stated as such in the registration. Either way, the DEV-B confirmation rule must be written and committed before the one DEV-B run. The LOSO estimate (+0.0029) suggests little winner's curse on DEV-A.

Even confirmed, the expected stage-1 effect is small: about +0.003 on all pairs and about +0.002 on good seeds. The good-seed boundary gap stays essentially open, with 63% of it still inside the ±2 px band.

I tested every pre-registered multimask variant on DEV-A only (3 300 pairs: 3 007 good seeds, 293 failing). The inputs were the logit dump (_e14_logitdump/geoset_rep_x_A) and _e13_dev/dev_pairs.json. I did not touch the TEST keyframe or DEV-B, and I modified no tracked files.

I wrote the grid, the metric and the selection rule to prereg_multimask.json before computing any variant mask or score. There are 10 candidate arms plus one GT oracle ceiling:
- **Select by predicted IoU:** I4 (best of tokens 0..3), I3 (best of tokens 1..3 only).
- **Select by stability:** S4 (best of 0..3), SF (stability used only for the existing fallback).
- **Select by agreement with the reprojected reference GT:** R4 (best of 0..3), RF (fallback only).
- **Average the hypotheses' logits:** M4 (mean of 4), M3 (mean of 1..3), W4 (mean weighted by predicted IoU).
- **Union:** X4 (max of the 4 logits).
- **Ceiling (uses GT):** O4, the best token per pair.

Every arm reuses the adopted path unchanged after choosing the 288 logits: the same upsampling, threshold 0, and exclusivity (xcl).

**Checks that the evaluation reproduces the adopted pipeline (all exact):**
- The control arm A0 reproduces the _e13_dev PNGs on all 170 views, and its J and F equal dev_pairs.json on all 3 300 pairs.
- My recomputed token-0 stability equals the dump's stored value everywhere.
- The reprojected reference masks reproduce decode_scene's own recorded round-1 reprojection overlap on 3 952/3 952 object-views (max difference 0).

**Result: decoder hypotheses do not address the good-seed boundary error.**
- The best arm moves good seeds by only +0.0005 (I3, CI −0.0006 to +0.0016). The good-seed gap is 0.0634.
- Even a GT oracle that picks the best of the 4 tokens per pair gains only +0.0068 on good seeds (CI 0.0055 to 0.0081), against +0.040 for the ±2 px band oracle. Most of its gain is on failing pairs (+0.056).
- The pre-registered rule picks **I3** overall: +0.0012 (CI +0.00002 to +0.0024). That gain comes from failing pairs (+0.0084).
  - I3's lower CI bound is fragile: it is above 0 for only 6 of 10 bootstrap seeds. I did not change the rule because of this; it is reported as a caveat.
  - I4 also qualifies and holds for all 10 seeds, but is smaller (+0.0008, CI +0.0001 to +0.0014).
- Stability selection, reference-agreement selection, and plain or IoU-weighted averaging are neutral or harmful on good seeds.
- The union arm (X4) is clearly harmful (−0.0106 on good seeds). It helps only objects of 100k px or more, consistent with the size-dependent coverage direction found in the boundary anatomy.

- For each eval camera it builds the zoomed output's logits L_z: the adopted output-resolution logits L, with the crop logits pasted where the zoom pasted (band ∩ window of each accepted object). It then applies run.exclusive_masks(L_z, 0.5).
- The crop pass is skipped on the cameras decoded only as memory candidates. Those outputs are never written, and no eval camera reads them.

The same GPU pass also produced:
- r2: geoset_rep, no zoom and no xcl
- z: geoset_rep_z2r, zoom only
- zxb: a diagnostic where the zoom decides which pixels are claimed but the round-2 logits decide who wins a contested pixel

Together with the adopted x, these four arms form a 2x2 factorial on DEV-A.

**Identity checks (all 85 frames pass).**
- The x arm recomputed in the job equals the adopted _e13_dev masks: 0 px difference over 3 952 object-views.
- Round-1 masks are 0 px different, with no missing or extra objects, and round1_conf.json is equal on 85 of 85 frames.
- The zoomed logits L_z thresholded at 0 equal the zoom output exactly.
- No zoom change lies outside the band.
- The claimant-argmax helper used for zxb reproduces exclusive_masks exactly.

**Results (dev_compare: scene-cluster bootstrap, views "t/cam", 10 000 resamples, seed 0).**
- **Composed arm vs adopted x.**
  - All pairs: ΔJ +0.0025, ΔF +0.0001; pair-mean J&F 0.9078 → 0.9103 (+0.0024); 11 scenes up, 5 down.
  - Good seeds: pair-mean 0.9366 → 0.9384. 1−recall gets worse (0.0637 → 0.0690) while 1−precision improves (0.0418 → 0.0314). The zoom pulls masks inward: 821 510 px added against 1 581 041 removed. Good seeds were already under-covered, so this goes the wrong way.
  - Failing seeds: pair-mean 0.6122 → 0.6215.
  - The gain sits in small objects: +0.0107 under 2k px, +0.0058 at 2k–10k, +0.0006 at 10k–100k, −0.0001 at 100k px or more.
- **The factorial.**
  - xcl alone: +0.0006 [+0.0001, +0.0011]. This is the first DEV-A measurement of E11.
  - Zoom alone: +0.0018 [−0.0003, +0.0039]. This is the first DEV-A measurement of E10 C2.
  - xcl added on top of zoom: +0.0001 [−0.0004, +0.0006].
  - Interaction (zx−z)−(x−r2): −0.0005 [−0.0009, −0.0002]; for good seeds −0.0007 [−0.0012, −0.0003].
  - So the two are less than additive: once the zoom has run, exclusivity adds nothing. The zoom has already removed some of the overlap xcl would resolve (contested pixels 1.917 M → 1.778 M), and xcl's recall loss stacks on the zoom's.
- **Diagnostic zxb.** Letting the round-2 logits pick the winner is worse than the crop logits: −0.0007 [−0.0013, −0.0003] vs the composed arm, −0.0063 on failing seeds. The natural composition is the better of the two.

**Cost.**
- The zoom ran 2 372 crops out of 3 338 non-empty eval-camera masks: 966 were too large for the window and skipped, 2 305 accepted.
- It took 517.5 s, 0.218 s per crop, about 3.0 s per eval view. The rest of the decode took 670.3 s, against the adopted 656.9 s.
- The composite and exclusivity step took ≤ 57.7 s. That figure includes three exclusivity variants plus the checks, so the composition alone costs less.
- Peak GPU memory was 12.4 GB.
- Job walls: decode groups 616, 579 and 515 s (including writing four arms' PNGs); dev_score 4 × about 168 s.
- In a full-camera pipeline the zoom cost scales with every target camera, not just the two eval cameras here.

implications: Zoom followed by xcl does not clear the bar on DEV-A. Against the adopted geoset_rep_x it gains +0.0013 [−0.0008, +0.0034] on all pairs and +0.0006 [−0.0012, +0.0026] on good seeds, and both CIs include 0. It also costs about 79% more decode time on the zoomed cameras.

It does not touch the good-seed boundary error, which was the target. On good seeds it closes only about 0.0018/0.0401 (4.5%) of the ±2 px band-oracle gap (pair means). It also moves the wrong way: the zoom pulls masks inward, so 1−recall worsens from 0.0637 to 0.0690 while 1−precision improves from 0.0418 to 0.0314. The anatomy found good seeds are under-covered and their misses are mostly unclaimed pixels.

The gain is in small objects (+0.0107 under 2k px) and failing seeds (+0.0092 pair-mean, mostly twin spill +0.04), and it comes from the zoom. That is a seed-failure or small-object effect, not a boundary-placement effect.

Zoom and xcl are less than additive. After the zoom, xcl adds +0.0001 [−0.0004, +0.0006]; on its own it adds +0.0006 [+0.0001, +0.0011] (interaction −0.0005 [−0.0009, −0.0002]). The zoom's inward pull already removes some of the overlap xcl resolves (contested pixels −7%), and xcl's recall loss stacks on the zoom's. Combining the two buys essentially nothing over zoom alone, and xcl-then-zoom (not run) has no reason to do better.

If a zoom is ever combined with exclusivity, the crop logits should decide contested pixels. The zxb variant, which uses the round-2 full-view logits instead, is −0.0007 [−0.0013, −0.0003] worse (−0.0063 on failing seeds).

measures.summary:
I estimated the E9 §5(b) arm (boundary-band BCE at a balanced weight W, IoU and object-score heads frozen) and its zero-dose control from the training logs plus DEV-A decodes of the existing trained checkpoints. I ran no training. The protocol was followed: TEST and DEV-B were never decoded, and no tracked file was changed.

GPU work: under the shared lock I decoded three checkpoints on DEV-A with the adopted path (gate reproj, xcl out), each with a round-2 logit dump. They are E9 D1 (decoder trained, W 0), E9 D2 (decoder plus band BCE at W 1) and E12 C0' (zero-dose retrain of the adopted recipe). A second pass of D1 and D2 also saved the token-0 logits and was byte-identical to the first (3 952 of 3 952 object-views per arm). The lock was held for about 1.65 h in total, and no job ran over 25 min.

**Expected effect: essentially zero.** I approximated intermediate doses by blending the D1 and D2 outputs; these two arms share the same per-step training samples in all 5 folds. Against its own W 0 control, the band arm at W 0.03 to 0.1 is expected to move DEV-A J&F by +0.0000 to +0.0006, and by the same amount on good seeds. No CI excludes 0.

For scale:
- A pure retrain moves DEV-A by +0.0017 [+0.0001, +0.0043].
- Shifting D1's threshold half a logit outward, with no training, gives +0.0031 [+0.0019, +0.0046].
- The ±2 px band gap on good seeds is 0.040.

The W 1 arm is confirmed harmful on DEV-A against its W 0 control: −0.0027 [−0.0055, +0.0000]; good seeds −0.0022 [−0.0039, −0.0004], with F −0.0035.

**Freezing the heads would not address the damage.** The IoU and object-score heads are not the channel:
- Presence flips are rare (14 of 3 300 pairs).
- D2's loss is in the token-0 boundary itself. Decoding both arms with token 0 forced still gives −0.0020, good seeds −0.0019 [−0.0035, −0.0004].
- D2's less confident boundary logits triple the stability fallback (111 → 393 of 3 300 pairs). That is a symptom, not the cause: forcing token 0 changes D2 by only +0.0001.

**Choice of W.** E9's "band term 10 to 20 times the base loss" is driven by rare spike steps from objects predicted absent, whose logits are fixed at −1024 and carry no gradient. Balancing gradient norms on DEV-A gives W of about 0.11 [0.095, 0.13]; balancing per-step median losses gives about 0.3. W 0.03 would make the band gradient only about a third of the base gradient.

**Leak: none.** In all 4 checkpoint sets, every scene's own fold model never saw that scene. The other folds' models train on every TEST frame (17/17), every DEV-A frame (85/85) and 85 of 255 DEV-B frames, but only of other scenes. That is the same status as the keyframe, so DEV-A is a fair yardstick. However, DEV-A shares the 17 scene clusters with TEST, so it is no sharper: a +0.0005 effect is below single-contrast CI half-widths of about 0.0013 to 0.0028.

**Cost.**
- Arm plus matched W 0 control: about 2 × 10.7k s of training (fold jobs run 32 to 40 min, so this needs a registered chain), plus about 2 × 11 to 12 min DEV-A decode, plus about 23 s host scoring. That is about 6.3 h for DEV-A.
- DEV-B confirm adds about 2 × 33 min and TEST about 2 × 8 min, for about 7.7 GPU h in all.
- Each extra W value adds about 3 h.
- Keeping E9's trainable set (heads unfrozen) lets the existing D1 serve as the exact zero-dose control, which halves training to about 3 h.

If registered anyway, set W from gradient balance: W of about 0.1 (W_grad 0.11 [0.095, 0.13] on DEV-A). The E9 §4 ratio of 10 to 20 times comes from spike steps of objects predicted absent, whose -1024 logits carry no gradient, so it should not be used. Freezing the IoU and object-score heads does not address the observed damage. Presence flips are rare (14 of 3 300), and D2's loss stays with token 0 forced (good seeds -0.0019 [-0.0035, -0.0004]). The heads' outputs would still move, because the shared decoder transformer and the memory attention are retrained from scratch. Holding decisions truly fixed needs a different arm: start from the adopted C0 fold checkpoints and train only the mask path (output_upscaling plus the token-0 hypernetwork MLP) with memory attention and the decoder transformer frozen. Cheapest faithful test: keep E9's trainable set and change only W. D1 is then an exact same-flow zero-dose control (identical per-step samples and step-1 loss in all 5 folds). That costs one training (about 3.0 h) plus a 12-min DEV-A decode, against about 6.3 h with a newly trained heads-frozen control.

DEV-A is leak-free for trained arms; their status is the same as the keyframe's. Each scene is decoded by a checkpoint that never saw it, and other folds' training on the scene's DEV and TEST frames does not touch its evaluation. But DEV-A is no sharper than TEST: it shares the 17 scene clusters and its retrain-noise CI is wider ([+0.0001, +0.0043] vs [+0.0001, +0.0030] on the keyframe). Every trained arm needs a same-code zero-dose control, and DEV-B's frames are interleaved in time with DEV-A's, so DEV-B is a weak independent check.

verdicts.recommendation:
Register exactly one arm: S1-E14, a global logit threshold offset on the final round-2 output. Frame it honestly as a logit seam fill / coverage calibration, not a good-seed boundary fix.

**Definition.** The preset is geoset_rep_x plus `pos = L > -0.5` on the final output logits. Exclusivity is `run.exclusive_masks(L + 0.5, 0.5)`. Round-1 masks, memory and upsampling are unchanged.

**Constant.** tau = +0.5, chosen on DEV-A only and declared as a deviation from the E14 exploratory argmax (+1). The reasons:
- a tighter CI: +0.0028 [+0.0013, +0.0047] vs +0.0031 [+0.0005, +0.0059];
- a smaller G2 risk: worst scene -0.0029 vs Dog -0.0091;
- LOSO picks {0.5, 1};
- replication on D1, where 0.5 gives +0.0031 [+0.0019, +0.0046] and the tightest CI.

**Order of steps.**
1. Implement the arm in tracked code.
2. Show that a DEV-A decode with the new preset reproduces the host emulation with 0 px difference.
3. Commit the registration with the DEV-B rule.
4. Decode DEV-B once, both the base geoset_rep_x_B and the arm from the same pass. The arm is post-decode, so a single dump gives both.

**DEV-B pass rule.** All rules are evaluated once. Bootstrap = dev_compare, hierarchical pair → view "t/cam" → scene, 10 000 resamples, seed 0.
- B1: ΔJ&F on all DEV-B pairs > 0, with 95% CI lower bound > 0.
- B2: point estimate in [+0.0010, +0.0050]. Below that is failure; above +0.0050 suggests a bug: stop and audit, do not report a result.
- B3: good-seed ΔJ&F (base J&F ≥ 0.8) ≥ 0 as a point estimate (non-harm on the target population), with its CI reported.
- B4: no scene below -0.005, and at most 3.5% of pairs drop by more than 0.01 (DEV-A: 2.4%).
- B5: mechanism invariants, which must hold exactly. If they fail it is a bug, not a result.
  - 0 px removed vs base;
  - at least 98% of added pixels were unclaimed at tau 0.

Failing any of B1–B4 closes the arm as 'no effect' and spends DEV-B. No other tau is tried and no TEST run follows.

**After a DEV-B pass.** Run the keyframe gate once (G1: CI lower bound > 0; G2: no scene below C0 - 0.01), with the prediction stated in the registration: keyframe ΔJ&F in [+0.0005, +0.0050], point estimate about +0.0025, G1 pass probability about 65%. Then run stage 2 under the unchanged adoption rule. The predicted basic Δ is about +0.05 to +0.40, from 66.7 × keyframe Δ × the E10/E11 ratios 0.52–2.0. Stage 2 is the main risk: the changes are spread out and 42% of the added pixels belong to other objects' GT, so the CI is likely E10-like.

**Do not register:**
- multimask I3/I4 (about +0.001, below gate resolvability);
- zoom→xcl (+0.0013, CI includes 0, wrong direction, +79% decode cost);
- any logit upsampler (all ≤ 0);
- E9 §5(b) band training (+0.0000 to +0.0006 expected, 6–8 GPU h).

**State plainly in ROADMAP/HANDOFF** that the good-seed ±2 px boundary gap (0.040 of 0.0634) remains essentially open. The best post-decode lever closes about 5% of it, so a real fix has to be model-level. One example is a decisions-frozen fine-tune of only the mask path, starting from the C0 checkpoints. That would need its own DEV-A ceiling estimate before any GPU-hours are committed.

arms.mechanism:
The exclusivity winner is the per-pixel argmax of L. Adding the same constant to every object does not change the argmax, so lowering the threshold to L > -0.5 can only add pixels where the gaining object is already the argmax. It cannot take a pixel from another mask that holds it, except through the nested-mask exemption.

Measured on DEV-A from the logit dump:
- 99.4% of the 12,108,305 added pixels were claimed by no mask at tau 0.
- No pixel is removed from any object.
- 1 exemption flip (non-exempt to exempt) out of 3,952 object-views.
- No mask goes from empty to non-empty.
- Empty-GT object-views that hold a mask stay at 60 (pixels 301,037 to 309,124).

So it fills the gaps between masks. Good-seed error pixels are 51% unclaimed misses and all come from the 0 threshold. The newly claimed pixels go to the right owner only 65.6% of the time: 29% land on another decoded object's GT and 6% on undecoded objects. It does not move boundaries between two decoded neighbours. Round-1 masks, memory encoding, the gate, the upsampler and the exclusivity cap are untouched.
arms.rule_and_constants:
In run.decode_scene, at the round-2 output of each target camera, in the branch `zoom is None and xcl != 'none'`:
- L = sam3_io.logits_to_original(out['logits_1008'], hw)[:, 0], unchanged from the adopted code.
- If xcl == 'outs': L += XCL_SHIFT, in place.
- keep = exclusive_masks(L, XCL_TAU_KEEP).

It follows that pos = L_orig > -0.5. The argmax is unchanged, with ties going to the lowest index. Exemption is computed on the shifted pos: lost >= 0.5 * |pos|. Absent objects sit at -1024 + 0.5 and are never positive.

XCL_SHIFT = 0.5 is a module constant, not a CLI knob. Everything else stays as adopted: θ 0.5, MIN_VALID 64, τ 0.7, k 3, OBJ_CHUNK 8, gate reproj, XCL_TAU_KEEP 0.5, zoom off, checkpoints geoset_pred_ft from each scene's own held-out fold.

How the constant was chosen (DEV-A only; declared in the registration as a deviation from the E14 exploratory argmax rule, which picked +1):
- Rule: take the largest DEV-A all-pair ΔJ&F among the taus that pass a keyframe-shaped G1 (CI lower bound > 0) and G2 (no scene < -0.01) on all 5 DEV-A pseudo-keyframes. A pseudo-keyframe is one DEV-A frame offset per scene, with 2 cameras and views = camera.
- tau 0.25 passes 5/5 (+0.0019).
- tau 0.5 passes 5/5 (+0.0028).
- tau 1 passes 4/5 (+0.0031). Offset +12 gives CI [-0.0010, +0.0059] and worst scene -0.0131.
- tau 1.5 passes 0/5.
- Taus 2 to 4 have smaller means.
- The pick is 0.5.
